claims.text: The assertion, with any ``<where> | <severity> | ...`` prefix stripped.
claims.why: The function splits on '|', checks if the second part is in _SEVERITIES, and returns the third part; otherwise returns raw. This matches the description.

claims.text: MEASURED: without this split, ``_resolve_store | medium | Mentions refusing paths under memory/ but code is truncated; the check may be missing`` was scored provably false because ``_resolve_store`` is defined -- but the finding never claimed otherwise. It is about a check INSIDE that function. Reading the location column as the subject manufactures a lie out of an honest observation.
claims.why: This claim references an example and a measurement outside the current chunk; the code here only implements the split logic.

claims.text: Decide whether one finding is provably wrong about the repository.
claims.why: The function returns verdicts 'false', 'false-elsewhere', 'scoped', or 'undecided' based on symbol presence, matching the description.

claims.text: Verdicts: ``false`` the named symbol is defined in the module it is claimed absent from
claims.why: The function checks if any named symbol (not imported) is in defined[module] and returns 'false' if so.

claims.text: ``false-elsewhere`` it exists, in another module -- wrong about WHERE, which is a different error needing a different repair
claims.why: The function checks if any named symbol exists in any module's defined set and returns 'false-elsewhere' if so.

claims.text: ``scoped`` the claim limits itself to the window its reader saw, so it asserts nothing about the program
claims.why: The function checks for _SELF_SCOPED pattern and returns 'scoped' if found.
The function returns 'undecided' in several cases (no existence claim, module not in index, symbol imported, no symbol resolved), indicating inability to decide.

claims.text: It can prove a finding false. It can never prove one true.
claims.why: The function only returns false/false-elsewhere for provably wrong findings; 'scoped' and 'undecided' are not proofs of truth.

observations.what: The function judge uses `_ABSENCE` and `_SELF_SCOPED` regex patterns that are not defined in this chunk; their behavior is assumed but cannot be verified here.
The function judge references `_SEVERITIES` (in claim_text) and `_NAME` (in candidate_names) which are not defined in this chunk; their correctness is assumed.
The function judge uses `defined.get(module)`; if module is not in defined, it returns 'undecided'. This means it cannot check claims about modules not in the index.
The function judge checks if a symbol is imported to avoid false positives, but this relies on the `imported` parameter being correctly populated.
